idiom_name: sealed interface + data class per rule + when expression without else
implementation_notes: Kotlin's sealed hierarchies plus when give a compiler-checked closed node set: a when over a sealed type needs no else and a new grammar rule breaks every evaluator at compile time. Since Kotlin 1.5 sealed interfaces may be implemented in the same package and compilation module (including other files), so the whole grammar can live next to the evaluator. Data classes give value equality and destructuring, which keeps nodes as plain data and operations outside them.
pitfalls: Sealed subtypes must stay in the same package and module, so consumers cannot add grammar rules: that is the trade for exhaustiveness.
A when used as a statement rather than an expression is not required to be exhaustive and silently ignores a new subtype; keep the evaluator an expression-valued when.
Data classes are shallowly immutable and their copy()/equals() walk the whole subtree, which is expensive on large trees and surprising when used as map keys.

variants.name: Abstract class with an overridden interpret per node
variants.idiom_name: abstract class Expression with abstract fun interpret(ctx) overridden per subclass
variants.implementation_notes: The Java-style realization, common in code ported from Java or in libraries that must let callers subclass the hierarchy: an abstract class declaring abstract fun interpret(ctx) and one subclass per rule overriding it. Dispatch lives in the node, so a new operation touches every subclass and nothing proves the set is complete; prefer the sealed form unless the node types must be open for subclassing outside the module, which sealed forbids.
pitfalls: Open classes invite subclassing from anywhere, so the node set grows without any evaluator noticing - exactly the guarantee sealed gives up.
Property initialisation order matters: a subclass that evaluates during construction can read child properties that are still null.
Abstract classes permit state, so per-node mutable fields creep in and make evaluation non-reentrant; prefer val-only nodes.
